sources.entry: LibreCAD - LibreCAD is a free Open Source CAD application for Windows, Apple and Linux. Support and documentation are free from our large, dedicated community of users, contributors and developers.

summary.one_liner: LibreCAD is a free, open-source 2D CAD drawing application for Windows, macOS and Linux, based on the community edition of QCAD and built with Qt.
summary.what_it_does: LibreCAD is a 2D CAD drawing tool built on the Qt cross-platform framework and derived from the community edition of QCAD. It is distributed under GPLv2 and its user interface is translated into over 30 languages. It can also run without opening the editor: the command-line converters dxf2pdf, dxf2png, dxf2svg, dwg2pdf, dwg2png, dwg2svg, dwg2dxf and dxf2dwg convert drawings, with options for paper size, resolution, fit-to-page, and DWG/DXF version selection. The README also describes native ESRI Shapefile (.shp) import, which brings in points, polylines, arcs and polygons, read-only. DWG input and output require a build with DWGSUPPORT enabled.
use_cases: convert DXF files to PDF, PNG or SVG
import ESRI Shapefiles into a CAD drawing
batch convert CAD drawings from the command line
open and edit DXF/DWG files on Windows, macOS or Linux
how_to_run: Download a release from the project's Releases page (or build from source with CMake or qmake)
Install Qt 6.4.0+ and Boost 1.55.0+ for building from source
librecad dxf2pdf -a -o drawing.pdf drawing.dxf (example command-line conversion)
stack: Qt (Qt 6.4.0+ for current branch; Qt 5.15 and Qt 5.2.1 for older branches)
notable: Command-line converters for DXF/DWG to PDF, PNG, SVG, DXF and DWG without opening the GUI
Built on libdxfrw for reading DXF and DWG files
Native ESRI Shapefile import with DBF-driven layers and styling
User interface translated into over 30 languages
Universal macOS build (Apple Silicon and Intel)
caveats: DWG input and output require a build with DWGSUPPORT enabled
The macOS builds are ad-hoc signed, not notarized, so Gatekeeper requires manual approval on first launch
Each branch needs a specific minimum Qt version; older Qt4 support ended with the 2.1 branch
Shapefile import is read-only; there is no Shapefile export
